title.zh: 卷20 列傳第12 王盟 賀蘭祥 尉遲綱 叱列伏龜 閻慶
title.en: Volume 20 Biographies 12: Wang Meng; He Lanxiang; Wei Chigang; Chilie Fugui; Yan Qing
title.raw: 卷20 列傳第12 王盟 賀蘭祥 尉遲綱 叱列伏龜 閻慶 Volume 20 Biographies 12: Wang Meng; He Lanxiang; Wei Chigang; Chilie Fugui; Yan Qing

sentences.zh: 王盟字子仵，明德皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Wang Meng, styled Ziwu, was elder brother of Empress Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng, styled Ziwu, was the elder brother of Empress Mingde.

sentences.zh: 其先樂浪人。

translations.literal: His forebears were men of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: His family came from Lelang.

sentences.zh: 六世祖波，前燕太宰。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Bo was grand preceptor of Former Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, Bo had been grand preceptor of Former Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖珍，魏黃門侍郎，贈幷州刺史、樂浪公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was yellow gate gentleman-attendant of Wei, posthumously awarded governor of Bing Province and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had served Wei as yellow gate gentleman-attendant and was posthumously made governor of Bing and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 父羆，伏波將軍，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Pi was general who crosses the waves; as a good-household youth he garrisoned Wuchuan and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pi, a general who crosses the waves, was posted to Wuchuan as a soldier of good family and made the town his home.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，破六汗拔陵攻陷諸鎮，盟亦為其所擁。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, Mohe Chen Bajie attacked and captured the garrison towns, and Meng too was swept up in his host.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Zhenguang era, Mohe Chen Bajie overran the frontier garrisons, and Wang Meng was swept up with his forces.

sentences.zh: 拔陵破後，流寓中山。

translations.literal: After Bajie was defeated, he wandered and lodged at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Bajie fell, he drifted to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除積射將軍，從蕭寶夤西征。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, he was appointed crossbow-shooting general and followed Xiao Baoyin on the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era he became crossbow-shooting general and marched west under Xiao Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 寶夤僭逆，盟遂逃匿民間，以觀其變。

translations.literal: When Baoyin usurped the throne, Meng thereupon hid among the common people to watch how affairs would turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled, Wang Meng went into hiding among the people to see how events would unfold.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱天光入關，盟出從之。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang entered the passes, Meng came out and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang entered the passes, Wang Meng came forward and joined him.

sentences.zh: 隨賀拔岳為前鋒，擒万俟醜奴，平秦隴，常先登力戰。

translations.literal: Following He Ba Yue as vanguard, he captured Wanqij Chounu, pacified Qin and Long, and was often first to scale the walls and fight hard.
translations.idiomatic: As vanguard under He Ba Yue he helped capture Wanqij Chounu and pacify Qin and Long, often first over the wall and fighting at the fore.

sentences.zh: 拜征西將軍、平秦郡守。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who campaigns west and governor of Pingqin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who campaigns west and governor of Pingqin commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖將討侯莫陳悅，徵盟赴原州以為留後大都督，鎮高平。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was about to attack Houmo Chen Yue, he summoned Meng to Yuan Province and made him rear-guard grand commander, garrisoning Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai prepared to attack Houmo Chen Yue, he summoned Wang Meng to Yuan Province, made him rear-guard grand commander, and posted him at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 悅平，除原州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, he was appointed governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmo Chen Yue was crushed, Wang Meng became governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武至長安，封魏昌縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei reached Chang'an, he was enfeoffed Duke of Weichang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang'an, Wang Meng was enfeoffed Duke of Weichang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，復加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he was further given grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he was further made grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 三年，徵拜司空，尋轉司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned and appointed minister of works, and soon transferred to minister over the masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled and made minister of works, then soon transferred to minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 迎魏文帝悼后於茹茹。

translations.literal: He welcomed Empress Ai, consort of Emperor Wen of Wei, from the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted Empress Ai, consort of Emperor Wen of Wei, back from the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，遷太尉。

translations.literal: He was given the added post attendant-in-ordinary and transferred to grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was given attendant-in-ordinary and promoted to grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝東征，以留後大都督行雍州事，節度關中諸軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei campaigned east, as rear-guard grand commander he acted as governor of Yong Province and directed all armies in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei marched east, Wang Meng stayed behind as rear-guard grand commander, acting governor of Yong, directing every army in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 趙青雀之亂，盟與開府李虎輔魏太子出頓渭北。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Zhao Qingque, Meng together with opening-office Li Hu supported the Wei crown prince out to encamp north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhao Qingque's rebellion, Wang Meng and Li Hu, opening-office, took the Wei crown prince and encamped north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 事平，進爵長樂郡公，增邑幷前二千戶，賜姓拓

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, his rank was advanced to Duke of Changle commandery, his fief together with the previous total reaching two thousand households, and he was granted the surname Tuo
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was put down, he was raised to Duke of Changle, his fief reaching two thousand households in all, and granted the surname Tuo

translations.literal: (ba)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: ba]

sentences.zh: 〔王〕氏。

translations.literal: [Wang] clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang.

sentences.zh: 東魏侵汾川，圍玉壁，盟以左軍大都督守蒲阪。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei invaded Fen River valley and besieged Yubi, Meng as left-army grand commander guarded Puyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei invaded the Fen valley and besieged Yubi, Wang Meng held Puyuan as left-army grand commander.

sentences.zh: 軍還，遷太保。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to grand protector.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was made grand protector.

sentences.zh: 九年，進位太傅，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, his rank was advanced to grand tutor, and he was given opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was raised to grand tutor and given opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 盟姿度弘雅，仁而泛愛。

translations.literal: Meng's bearing was broad and refined; he was benevolent and universally loving.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng carried himself with broad refinement, benevolent and open-handed toward all.

sentences.zh: 雖位居師傅，禮冠群后，而謙恭自處，未嘗以勢位驕人。

translations.literal: Though his rank stood as grand tutor, his ritual precedence above the consorts, he kept himself humble and never used power and position to lord it over others.
translations.idiomatic: Though he ranked as grand tutor, above the consorts in ritual precedence, he remained humble and never flaunted power or rank.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝甚尊重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 及有疾，數幸其第，親問所欲。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, the emperor repeatedly visited his residence and personally asked what he wished.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the emperor visited his home again and again and asked in person what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 其見禮如此。

translations.literal: Such was the honor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor he received.

sentences.zh: 大統十一年，薨，贈本官，諡曰孝定。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Datong he died; his former offices were posthumously confirmed, and his posthumous title was Xiaoding.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 11 he died; his offices were posthumously confirmed, and he was given the posthumous title Xiaoding.

sentences.zh: 子勵，字丑興，性忠果，有才幹。

translations.literal: His son Li, styled Chouxing, was by nature loyal and resolute and had talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Li, styled Chouxing, was loyal and resolute by nature, with real talent and drive.

sentences.zh: 年十七，從太祖入關，及太祖平秦隴，定關中，勵常侍從。

translations.literal: At seventeen he followed the Grand Progenitor in entering the passes; when the Grand Progenitor pacified Qin and Long and settled Guanzhong, Li was constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai through the passes; when Yuwen Tai pacified Qin and Long and secured Guanzhong, Wang Li was constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂之曰：「為將，坐見成敗者上也，被堅執銳者次也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once said to him: "As a general, one who sits and sees victory and defeat is of the highest sort; one who dons armor and grasps sharp blades is next.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once told him: "The best general reads the field from afar; the next best fights in the front line.

sentences.zh: 」勵曰：「意欲兼之。

translations.literal: " Li said: "I mean to combine both.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Li said: "I aim to do both.

sentences.zh: 」太祖大笑。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 尋拜平東將軍、散騎常侍，賜爵梁甫縣公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed general who pacifies the east and attendant of scattered cavalry, and enfeoffed Duke of Liangfu county.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general who pacifies the east and attendant of scattered cavalry, and enfeoffed Duke of Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 大統初，為千牛備身直長、領左右，出入臥內，小心謹肅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he served as captain of the thousand-ox bodyguard and commander of the left and right guard, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters, careful, cautious, and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he became captain of the thousand-ox bodyguard and commander of the left and right guard, passing in and out of the inner quarters with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝嘗曰：「王勵可謂不二心之臣也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei once said: "Wang Li may be called a minister of undivided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei once said: "Wang Li is a minister without a second heart.

sentences.zh: 」沙苑之役，勵以都督領禁兵從太祖。

translations.literal: " At the battle of Shayuan, Li as area commander led the forbidden troops and followed the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: " At Shayuan, Wang Li commanded the forbidden troops under Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 勵居左翼，與帳下數十人用短兵接戰，當其前者，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Li held the left wing; with several dozen men of his personal guard he joined close combat with short weapons, and those who faced him suffered many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Li held the left wing; with a few dozen household troops he fought hand to hand, and those who met him fell in heaps.

sentences.zh: 勵亦被傷重，遂卒于行間，時年二十六。

translations.literal: Li too was heavily wounded and thereupon died on the field; he was twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Li was badly wounded himself and died on the field, aged twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 太祖深悼焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、太尉、領尚書令、十州諸軍事、雍州刺史，追封咸陽郡公，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded bearer of the staff, grand commandant, concurrent director of the masters of writing, military affairs of ten provinces, and governor of Yong Province; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Xianyang commandery; posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given bearer of the staff, grand commandant, director of the masters of writing, command over ten provinces, and governor of Yong; raised after death to Duke of Xianyang with the posthumous title Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 子弼襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Bi succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Bi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 尚魏安樂公主，官至撫軍將軍、大都督、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He married Princess Anle of Wei; his offices reached general who pacifies the army, grand commander, and unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Anle of Wei and rose to general who pacifies the army, grand commander, and unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 懋性溫和，小心敬慎。

translations.literal: Mao was gentle in nature, careful and reverently cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi was gentle by nature, careful and reverently cautious.

sentences.zh: 宿衛宮禁，十有餘年，勤恪當官，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: He guarded the palace precincts for more than ten years, diligent and conscientious in office, and never had a fault.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he guarded the palace precincts, diligent in duty and without a single fault.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，除南岐州刺史，進爵安寧郡公，增邑幷前二千戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Deposed Emperor, he was appointed governor of South Qishan Province, advanced in rank to Duke of Anning commandery, and his fief together with the previous total reached two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Deposed Emperor's second year he became governor of South Qishan, was raised to Duke of Anning, and his fief reached two thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，遷大將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was transferred to grand general and grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gong of Wei's second year he was made grand general and grand commander.

sentences.zh: 後拜小司寇。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed junior minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed junior minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 卒于官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子悅嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yue succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Yue succeeded.

sentences.zh: 官至大將軍、同州刺史，改封濟南郡公。

translations.literal: His offices reached grand general and governor of Tong Province; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jinan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand general and governor of Tong, and his title was changed to Duke of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 王子顯

translations.literal: Wang Zixian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zixian

sentences.zh: 盟兄子顯，幼而敏悟，沉靜少言。

translations.literal: Meng's elder brother's son Zixian from youth was quick and perceptive, calm and reticent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng's nephew Wang Zixian was clever and quick-witted from boyhood, calm and sparing of speech.

sentences.zh: 初為太祖帳內都督，累遷奉車都尉、寧朔將軍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、燕朔顯蔚四州諸軍事、燕州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、光祿卿、鳳州刺史，賜爵洛邑縣公，進位大將軍，卒。

translations.literal: At first he was a commander within the Grand Progenitor's tent; he was progressively transferred to chariot-court commandant, general of pacifying the north, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, military affairs of the four provinces of Yan, Shuo, Xian, and Wei, governor of Yan Province, grand general of swift cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, director of the imperial household, and governor of Feng Province; enfeoffed Duke of Luoyi county; advanced in rank to grand general; and died.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commander in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's tent and rose through chariot-court commandant, general of pacifying the north, grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol, commander of Yan, Shuo, Xian, and Wei, governor of Yan, grand general of swift cavalry with opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, director of the imperial household, and governor of Feng; was enfeoffed Duke of Luoyi, raised to grand general, and died.

sentences.zh: 子誼嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 誼倜儻有大志，深為高祖所親委。

translations.literal: Yi was free-spirited and had great ambition, and was deeply trusted and entrusted by the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was bold and high-minded, and won the deep trust of High Ancestor Yuwen Yong.

sentences.zh: 少歷顯職，見重於時。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through prominent offices and was valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held conspicuous posts and was respected in his time.

sentences.zh: 位至柱國、平陽郡公。

translations.literal: His rank reached pillar of state and Duke of Pingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to pillar of state and Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 宣帝卽位，進封揚國公，拜大司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Yang state and appointed grand minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was raised to Duke of Yang and made grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 大象末，襄州總管、上柱國。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was governor-general of Xiang Province and upper pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was governor-general of Xiang and upper pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭祥

translations.literal: He Lanxiang
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang

sentences.zh: 賀蘭祥字盛樂。

translations.literal: He Lanxiang, styled Shengle.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang, styled Shengle.

sentences.zh: 其先與魏俱起，有紇伏者，為賀蘭莫何弗，因以為氏。

translations.literal: His forebears rose together with Wei; there was Gefuzhe, who was Helan mohefu, and they took that as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had risen with Wei; an ancestor named Gefuzhe had been a Helan mohefu, and from that came their surname.

sentences.zh: 其後有以良家子鎮武川者，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Later there were those who, as good-household youths, garrisoned Wuchuan, and there they settled their families.
translations.idiomatic: Later some of the clan were posted to Wuchuan as soldiers of good family and made the town their home.

sentences.zh: 父初真，少知名，為鄉閭所重。

translations.literal: His father Chuzhen from youth was known by name and was respected by village and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuzhen was known from youth and respected throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 尚太祖姊建安長公主。

translations.literal: He married the Grand Progenitor's elder sister, Princess Jian'an the Long.
translations.idiomatic: He married Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's elder sister, Princess Jian'an the Long.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，追贈太傅、柱國、常山郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he was posthumously awarded grand tutor, pillar of state, and Duke of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 2 he was posthumously made grand tutor, pillar of state, and Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 祥年十一而孤，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: Xiang at eleven lost his father; in mourning he observed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang was orphaned at eleven and observed the mourning rites properly.

sentences.zh: 長於舅氏，特為太祖所愛。

translations.literal: He grew up in his maternal uncle's house and was especially loved by the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in his uncle's household, he was especially cherished by Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 雖在戎旅，常博延儒士，教以書傳。

translations.literal: Though in the army, he often broadly gathered Confucian scholars and had them taught the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Even on campaign he gathered Confucian scholars and had them taught the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太祖初入關，祥與晉公護俱在晉陽，後乃遣使迎致之，語在《護傳》。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first entered the passes, Xiang together with Duke of Jin Hu were both at Jinyang; only later did he send envoys to welcome and bring them; the account is in the Biography of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai first entered the passes, He Lanxiang and Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu were both at Jinyang; only later did he send envoys to fetch them—the account is in the Biography of Hu.

sentences.zh: 年十七，解褐奉朝請，加威烈將軍。

translations.literal: At seventeen he left office and became supernumerary attendant at court, given the added rank general of awesome might.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he entered service as supernumerary attendant at court and was given the added title general of awesome might.

sentences.zh: 祥少有膽氣，志在立功。

translations.literal: Xiang from youth had courage and spirit and aspired to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth He Lanxiang had courage and aimed to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 尋擢補都督，恆在帳下。

translations.literal: Soon he was selected and appointed commander, always in the tent staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon chosen and made a commander, always serving in the headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 從平侯莫陳悅，又迎魏孝武。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Houmo Chen Yue and again welcomed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Houmo Chen Yue and later escorted Emperor Xiaowu of Wei west.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，封撫夷縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For his earlier and later achievements he was enfeoffed Baron of Fuyi county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his cumulative service he was enfeoffed Baron of Fuyi with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍從擊潼關，獲東魏將薛長孺。

translations.literal: He still followed in attacking Tong Pass and captured Eastern Wei general Xue Changru.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the attack on Tong Pass and captured Eastern Wei general Xue Changru.

sentences.zh: 又攻回洛城，拔之。

translations.literal: He again attacked Huiluo city and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Huiluo city next and took it.

sentences.zh: 還，拜左右直長，進爵為公，增邑幷前一千三百戶。

translations.literal: On returning, he was appointed left and right direct captain, advanced in nobility to duke, and his fief together with the previous total reached one thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made left and right direct captain, raised to duke, and his fief reached one thousand three hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，從儀同于謹攻楊氏壁，祥先登，克之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, following acting-three-division Yu Jin in attacking Yangshi Rampart, Xiang was first to ascend and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 3, following Yu Jin in the attack on Yangshi Rampart, He Lanxiang was first over the wall and took it.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛將軍，加持節、征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right guard general, given the added credentials bearer of the staff and general who captures the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right guard general with bearer of the staff and general who captures the enemy.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，詔祥留衛京師。

translations.literal: At the battle of Shayuan, an edict ordered Xiang to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Shayuan he was ordered by edict to stay and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 後以留守功，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Later, for his merit in holding the capital, his fief was increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for guarding the capital, he received eight hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 尋除鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed general who garrisons the west.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general who garrisons the west.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏文帝東伐，祥領軍從戰河橋，以功加使持節、大都督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Emperor Wen of Wei campaigned east, Xiang led troops and followed in fighting at Heqiao; for merit he was given bearer of the staff and grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Emperor Wen of Wei marched east, He Lanxiang led troops to Heqiao and, for his service, received bearer of the staff and grand commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, and attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol and attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 九年，從太祖與東魏戰於邙山，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he followed the Grand Progenitor in fighting Eastern Wei at Mount Mang; his rank was advanced to grand general of swift cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and he was given the added post attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai against Eastern Wei at Mount Mang, was raised to grand general of swift cavalry with opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and given attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除都督三荊南襄南雍平信江隨二郢淅十二州諸軍事、荊州刺史，進爵博陵郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was appointed commander of military affairs in the twelve provinces of Three Jing, South Xiang, South Yong, Ping, Xin, Jiang, Sui, Two Ying, and Xi, and governor of Jing Province; his nobility was advanced to Duke of Boling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made commander of military affairs in twelve provinces—Three Jing, South Xiang, South Yong, Ping, Xin, Jiang, Sui, the two Ying, and Xi—and governor of Jing, and was raised to Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 先是，祥嘗行荊州事，雖未期月，頗有惠政，至是重往，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiang had once acted as governor of Jing Province; though not a full month had passed, he had quite benevolent policies; when he now went again, the common people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang had briefly governed Jing before; though less than a month in office, his rule had already been benevolent, and when he returned the people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 由是漢南流民，襁負而至者日有千數。

translations.literal: From this, refugees south of the Han, carrying infants on their backs, arrived by the day in thousands.
translations.idiomatic: From then on refugees south of the Han came by the thousand each day, infants bound to their backs.

sentences.zh: 遠近蠻夷，莫不款附。

translations.literal: Barbarians near and far all came submitting in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes near and far all came in willing submission.

sentences.zh: 祥隨機撫納，咸得其歡心。

translations.literal: Xiang as the occasion required reassured and received them, and all obtained his goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang received and reassured them as each case required, winning every heart.

sentences.zh: 時盛夏亢陽，祥乃親巡境內，觀政得失。

translations.literal: At the time, in the height of summer there was severe drought; Xiang thereupon personally toured within his borders to observe the gains and losses of government.
translations.idiomatic: That summer brought fierce drought; He Lanxiang then toured his jurisdiction in person to see where governance had failed.

sentences.zh: 見有發掘古冢，暴露骸骨者，乃謂守令曰：「此豈仁者之為政耶。

translations.literal: Seeing ancient tombs dug open and skeletons left exposed, he said to the magistrates and commandants: "Is this the governance of a benevolent man?
translations.idiomatic: When he found old graves robbed and bones left exposed, he told the local magistrates: "Is this how a benevolent man governs?

sentences.zh: 」於是命所在收葬之，卽日澍雨。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the localities to gather and bury them, and that very day soaking rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the local authorities to collect and rebury the remains, and that same day a soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大有年。

translations.literal: That year there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a bumper harvest.

sentences.zh: 州境先多古墓，其俗好行發掘，至是遂息。

translations.literal: Within the province there had long been many ancient tombs, and the custom favored grave-robbing; from this time it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The province had long held many ancient tombs and a custom of grave-robbing, which now ceased.

sentences.zh: 祥雖太祖密戚，性甚清素。

translations.literal: Though Xiang was a close kinsman of the Grand Progenitor, his nature was very plain and austere.
translations.idiomatic: Though He Lanxiang was a close kinsman of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, he lived plainly and without ostentation.

sentences.zh: 州境南接襄陽，西通岷蜀，物產所出，多諸珍異。

translations.literal: The province bordered Xiangyang to the south and connected with Min and Shu to the west; what its lands produced included many rare and unusual goods.
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered Xiangyang in the south and opened west to Min and Shu, and its lands yielded many rare goods.

sentences.zh: 時旣與梁通好，行李往來，公私贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: At the time relations with Liang were friendly; travelers came and went, and whether public or private gifts, he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Relations with Liang were then friendly and travelers passed back and forth, but he accepted no gifts, public or private.

sentences.zh: 梁雍州刺史、岳陽王蕭詧，欽其節儉，乃以竹屏風、絺綌之屬及以經史贈之。

translations.literal: Liang's governor of Yong Province and Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, admired his frugality and thereupon sent him bamboo screens, fine hemp cloth, and the like, together with classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha, Liang governor of Yong and Prince of Yueyang, admired his thrift and sent bamboo screens, fine hemp cloth, and sets of classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 祥難違其意，取而付諸所司。

translations.literal: Xiang, finding it hard to go against his intent, took them and handed them over to the appropriate office.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to spurn the gesture outright, He Lanxiang accepted the gifts and turned them over to the proper office.

sentences.zh: 太祖後聞之，並以賜祥。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor later heard of it and bestowed them all on Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai learned of this, he had everything sent on to He Lanxiang.

sentences.zh: 尋被徵還。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 十六年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was appointed grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 太祖以涇渭溉灌之處，渠堰廢毀，乃命祥脩造富平堰，開渠引水，東注於洛。

translations.literal: Because the places irrigated by the Jing and Wei had ruined canals and dikes, the Grand Progenitor ordered Xiang to repair and build the Fuping weir, open a canal to draw water, and send it east to pour into the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Jing and Wei were used for irrigation, canals and dikes had fallen into ruin, so Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai put He Lanxiang in charge of rebuilding the Fuping weir, opening a canal, and sending water east into the Luo.

sentences.zh: 功用旣畢，民獲其利。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, the people reaped the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done, the people benefited.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，行華州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed Emperor of Wei, he acted in Hua Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the deposed Wei emperor he acted as governor of Hua.

sentences.zh: 後改華州為同州，仍以祥為刺史。

translations.literal: Later Hua Province was changed to Tong Province, and Xiang was still made its governor.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was later renamed Tong, and He Lanxiang remained its governor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed left vice director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授小司馬。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was given junior minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he was made junior minister of war.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐祚，進位柱國，遷大司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced in rank to pillar of state and transferred to grand minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded he was raised to pillar of state and made grand minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護執政，祥與護中表，少相親愛，軍國之事，護皆與祥參謀。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Jin Hu held power; Xiang and Hu were cousins by marriage and from youth had been close; in military and state affairs Hu always consulted with Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: While Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power, he and He Lanxiang—cousins by marriage and friends from youth—planned military and state affairs together.

sentences.zh: 及誅趙貴，廢孝閔帝，祥有力焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao Gui was executed and Emperor Xiaomin was deposed, Xiang had a hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang helped when Zhao Gui was killed and Emperor Xiaomin was deposed.

sentences.zh: 武成初，吐谷渾侵涼州，詔祥與宇文貴總兵討之。

translations.literal: At the start of Wucheng, Tuyuhun invaded Liang Province; an edict ordered Xiang together with Yuwen Gui to command troops to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wucheng, when Tuyuhun invaded Liang Province, He Lanxiang and Yuwen Gui were ordered to take command against them.

sentences.zh: 祥乃遣其軍司檄吐谷渾曰：

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon sent his army marshal to issue a proclamation to Tuyuhun, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang sent his army marshal to proclaim to Tuyuhun:

sentences.zh: 夫二氣旣分，三才定位，樹之以君，本為黔首，豈使悖義違道，肆於民上？

translations.literal: When yin and yang were already divided and heaven, earth, and man had taken their places, rulers were set over the people for the sake of the common folk—how could one allow rebellion against righteousness and violation of the Way, and act wantonly over the people?
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang were divided and heaven, earth, and man had taken their places, rulers were established for the people's sake—how could one rebel against righteousness, violate the Way, and lord it over the people?

sentences.zh: 昔魏氏不綱，群方幅裂，豺狼橫噬，龜玉已毀，喁喁黔黎，咸墜塗炭。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei lost the reins; the regions split apart; wolves and jackals ravaged at will; the royal jade was shattered; the common people, clamoring, all fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei lost control, the realm splintered, predators ravaged unchecked, the royal jade was shattered, and the people fell into misery.

sentences.zh: 我先皇神武應期，一匡天下，東戡南剪，無思不服。

translations.literal: Our late emperor, divinely martial, answered the age; he set the realm right in one stroke; east he conquered, south he cut down, and none who thought of resisting submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Our late emperor, divinely martial, answered the age, set the realm right at a stroke, conquered east and south, and left none who thought to resist unsubdued.

sentences.zh: 天鑒有周，世篤英聖，遂廓洪基，奄荒萬宇。

translations.literal: Heaven looked upon Zhou; generation after generation it has been rich in heroic sages; thus the great foundation was cleared and the ten thousand regions were embraced.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favored Zhou; generation after generation it produced heroic sages, cleared the great foundation, and embraced the ten thousand regions.

sentences.zh: 固則神皋西嶽，險則百二猶在。

translations.literal: Where it was firm stood the sacred lands and western peaks; where it was perilous, the hundred passes still held.
translations.idiomatic: Where the land was firm stood the sacred heartland and western peaks; where it was perilous, the hundred passes still held.

sentences.zh: 卿士師師，羣后率職。

translations.literal: Ministers and grandees led in good order; the host of lords performed their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and grandees led in good order, and the host of lords performed their duties.

sentences.zh: 故知三靈之所睠集，四隩之所來蘇也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the three spirits have turned their gaze here, and the four corners have come back to life.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows the three spirits have turned their favor here and the four corners of the earth have revived.

sentences.zh: 彼國世在西垂，作藩于魏。

translations.literal: Your state for generations has been in the western marches, serving Wei as a frontier domain.
translations.idiomatic: Your state has for generations dwelt in the western marches as a frontier domain of Wei.

sentences.zh: 值中原政亂，遂阻皇風，首鼠兩端，伺我邊隙。

translations.literal: When the central plains fell into disorder, you blocked the imperial wind; you played both sides; you watched for gaps on our borders.
translations.idiomatic: When the central plains fell into disorder you blocked the imperial wind, played both sides, and watched for gaps on our borders.

sentences.zh: 先皇含垢藏疾，仍存聘享，欲睦之以鄰好，申之以婚姻。

translations.literal: The late emperor swallowed insult and hid his injury, yet still maintained embassies and tribute, wishing to bind you with neighborly friendship and seal it with marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor swallowed insult and hid his injury, yet still maintained embassies and tribute, hoping to bind you in neighborly friendship and marriage.

sentences.zh: 彼國苞藏禍心，屢違盟約，外結仇讐，自貽近患，是故往年致突厥之師也。

translations.literal: Your state harbored a treacherous heart, repeatedly violated treaties, allied abroad with enemies, and brought near calamity on itself—therefore in former years we brought the Turks' army.
translations.idiomatic: Your state harbored treachery, broke treaties again and again, allied abroad with enemies, and brought calamity on itself—hence the Turkish army of former years.

sentences.zh: 自爾迄今，蜂蠆彌毒，入我姑臧，俘我河縣，芟夷我菽麥，虔劉我蒼生。

translations.literal: From then until now the sting has grown ever more venomous: you entered our Guzang, captured our He county, cut down our millet and wheat, and slaughtered our people.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the sting has grown ever more venomous: you entered our Guzang, captured He county, cut down our millet and wheat, and slaughtered our people.

sentences.zh: 我皇武以止戈，文以懷遠，德覃四海，化溢八荒。

translations.literal: Our emperor uses martial power to stop war and civil virtue to win the distant; his virtue spreads through the four seas and his transforming influence overflows the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor uses martial power to stop war and civil virtue to win the distant; his virtue fills the four seas and his transforming influence overflows the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 以彼惡稔禍盈，故命龔行九伐。

translations.literal: Because your wickedness was ripe and your calamities full, he ordered the punitive expedition of nine campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Because your wickedness was ripe and your calamities full, he ordered the punitive expedition of nine campaigns.

sentences.zh: 武臣猛將，天張雷動，皆六郡良家，三秦精銳，揮戈擐甲，同萃龍沙。

translations.literal: Warrior ministers and fierce generals, heaven-stretched and thunder-shaken, all were good families of the six commanderies and elite troops of the three Qins; they swung spears and donned armor and gathered together at Longsha.
translations.idiomatic: Warrior ministers and fierce generals, heaven-stretched and thunder-shaken, all drawn from good families of the six commanderies and elite troops of the three Qins, swung spears, donned armor, and gathered at Longsha.

sentences.zh: 柱國、博陵公祥，貴戚重望，乃文乃武，受脤廟堂，元戎啟路；

translations.literal: Pillar of state and Duke of Boling Xiang, a kinsman of weighty repute, both civil and martial, received the sacrificial meat in the ancestral temple and opened the way as commander-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of state and Duke of Boling He Lanxiang, a kinsman of weighty repute, both civil and martial, received the sacrificial meat in the ancestral temple and opened the way as commander-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 太傅、燕國公

translations.literal: Grand tutor and Duke of Yan
translations.idiomatic: Grand tutor and Duke of Yan

translations.literal: (Yu)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: yu]

sentences.zh: 謹，英猷不世，應變無窮，仗旄指麾，為其謀主；

translations.literal: Jin, with strategy unmatched in the age, inexhaustible in adapting to change, bearing the banner and directing the host, was chief strategist;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, with strategy unmatched in the age and inexhaustible in adapting to change, bearing the banner and directing the host, was chief strategist;

sentences.zh: 柱國、化政公貴，早播威聲，奇正兼設，直取龍涸，濟自南河。

translations.literal: Pillar of state and Duke of Huazheng Gui, who early spread his martial renown, combined orthodox and unorthodox tactics, took Longge straight, and crossed from the South River.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of state and Duke of Huazheng Yuwen Gui, who early spread his martial renown, combined orthodox and unorthodox tactics, took Longge straight, and crossed from the South River.

sentences.zh: 突厥與國睦親，同恥反道，驅引弓之民，總穹廬之衆，解鞍成山，雲蒸霧合。

translations.literal: The Turks are in friendly kinship with our state, sharing shame at rebellion against the Way; they drive bow-bearing peoples and gather the hosts of the felt tents; saddles unhitched pile like mountains; clouds of steam and mist combine.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are in friendly kinship with our state and share shame at rebellion against the Way; they drive bow-bearing peoples and gather the hosts of the felt tents; saddles unhitched pile like mountains as clouds of steam and mist combine.

sentences.zh: 往歲王師西伐，成都不守；

translations.literal: In former years the royal army campaigned west; Chengdu did not hold;
translations.idiomatic: In former years the royal army marched west and Chengdu did not hold;

sentences.zh: 桴鼓南臨，江陵底定。

translations.literal: drums and bells pressed south; Jiangling was settled to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: drums and bells pressed south and Jiangling was settled to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 鑿空萬里，辟地千都，荒服畏威，膜拜厥角。

translations.literal: They opened empty lands ten thousand li away and carved out territories of a thousand capitals; the wild borderlands feared their might and bowed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: They opened empty lands ten thousand li away and carved out territories of a thousand capitals; the wild borderlands feared their might and bowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 成敗之機，較然可見。

translations.literal: The hinge of victory and defeat is clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: The hinge of victory and defeat is clearly visible.

sentences.zh: 若能轉禍為福，深識事宜，君臣相率，輿櫬稽顙，則爵等顯除，永蕃西服；

translations.literal: If you can turn calamity into blessing, deeply recognize what the times require, and ruler and ministers together come bearing coffins and kowtow in submission, then ranks and titles will be clearly removed and you will forever guard the western domains;
translations.idiomatic: If you can turn calamity into blessing, deeply recognize what the times require, and ruler and ministers together come bearing coffins and kowtow in submission, then ranks and titles will be removed and you will forever guard the western domains;

sentences.zh: 如其徘徊危邦，覬延時漏，覆宇湮祀，良助寒心。

translations.literal: if you linger in a perilous state, hoping to prolong your time, and overturn your realm and extinguish your sacrifices, you will only deepen our cold resolve.
translations.idiomatic: if you linger in a perilous state, hoping to prolong your time, and overturn your realm and extinguish your sacrifices, you will only deepen our cold resolve.

sentences.zh: 幸思嘉謀，以圖去就。

translations.literal: Consider good counsel and decide whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Consider good counsel and decide whether to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 遂與吐渾廣定王、鐘留王等戰，破之。

translations.literal: He thereupon fought the Tuyuhun princes Guangding and Zhongliu and others, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He then fought the Tuyuhun princes Guangding and Zhongliu and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 因拔其洮陽、

translations.literal: He then captured their Taoyang and
translations.idiomatic: He then captured their Taoyang and

translations.literal: (Gong)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: gong]

sentences.zh: 〔洪〕和二城，以其地為洮州。

translations.literal: [Hong] and Er counties, and made the territory Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Er counties and made the territory Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 撫安西土，振旅而還。

translations.literal: He pacified and reassured the western lands and returned with his army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the western lands and returned with his army in good order.

sentences.zh: 進封涼國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Liang state with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Liang with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 保定

translations.literal: Baoding
translations.idiomatic: Baoding

translations.literal: (Four)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: four]

sentences.zh: 年薨，年四十八。

translations.literal: He died in that year, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、太師、同岐等十二州諸軍事、同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded bearer of the staff, grand tutor, military affairs of twelve provinces including Tong and Qi, and governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given bearer of the staff, grand tutor, command over twelve provinces including Tong and Qi, and governor of Tong.

sentences.zh: 諡曰景。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jing.

sentences.zh: 有七子，敬讓璨師寬知名。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Jing, Rang, Can, Shi, and Kuan were well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Jing, Rang, Can, Shi, and Kuan were well known.

sentences.zh: 敬少歷顯職，封化隆縣侯。

translations.literal: Jing in youth passed through eminent posts and was enfeoffed Marquis of Hualong county.
translations.idiomatic: Jing in youth held eminent posts and was enfeoffed Marquis of Hualong.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵涼國公，位至柱國大將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Liang state and rose to pillar-of-state grand general and governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the ducal title of Liang, rose to pillar-of-state grand general, and became governor of Hua.

sentences.zh: 讓，大將軍、鄜州刺史、河東郡公。

translations.literal: Rang was grand general, governor of Fu Province, and Duke of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rang was grand general, governor of Fu, and Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 璨，開府儀同三司、宜陽縣公。

translations.literal: Can was opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol and Duke of Yiyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Can held opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol and was Duke of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 〔建德五年，從高祖于幷州，戰歿，贈上大將軍，追封清都郡公。

translations.literal: [In Jiande fifth year, following Emperor Wen at Bing Province, he died in battle, posthumously awarded upper grand general, and posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Qingdu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: [In Jiande fifth year Can followed Emperor Wen at Bing Province, fell in battle, and was posthumously made upper grand general and Duke of Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 師，尚世宗女，位至上儀同大將軍、幽州刺史、博陵郡公。

translations.literal: Shi married Shizong's daughter and rose to upper equal-to-three-division grand general, governor of You Province, and Duke of Boling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi married Emperor Xiaoming's daughter and rose to upper equal-to-three-division grand general, governor of You, and Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 寬，開府儀同大將軍、武始郡公。

translations.literal: Kuan was opening-office equal-to-three-division grand general and Duke of Wuzhi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was opening-office equal-to-three-division grand general and Duke of Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 祥弟隆，大將軍、襄樂縣公。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Long was grand general and Duke of Xiangle county.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanxiang's younger brother Long was grand general and Duke of Xiangle.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝與祥有舊，開皇初，追贈上柱國。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui had old ties with Xiang; at the start of Kaihuang he was posthumously awarded upper pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui had old ties with He Lanxiang and posthumously made him upper pillar of state at the start of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 尉遲綱

translations.literal: Wei Chigang
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chigang

sentences.zh: 綱驍果有膂力，善騎射。

translations.literal: Gang was fierce and resolute, had bodily strength, and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chigang was fierce and strong, and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚寵之，委以心膂。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor greatly favored him and entrusted him as a trusted aide.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai greatly favored him and trusted him as a close aide.

sentences.zh: 河橋之戰，太祖馬中流矢，因而驚奔。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao, the Grand Progenitor's horse was struck by a flying arrow and thereupon bolted in panic.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Heqiao, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's horse was struck by a flying arrow and bolted in panic.

sentences.zh: 綱與李穆等左右力戰，衆皆披靡，太祖方得乘馬。

translations.literal: Gang with Li Mu and others fought hard on either side; the masses all were routed; only then did the Grand Progenitor manage to mount a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chigang and Li Mu and others fought hard on either side until the enemy broke; only then could Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai remount.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，增邑八百戶，進爵為公，仍拜平遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: For his earlier and later merit, his fief was increased by eight hundred households, his nobility was advanced to duke, and he was appointed general who pacifies the distant and infantry commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For his earlier and later service he received eight hundred more households, was raised to duke, and was made general who pacifies the distant and infantry commandant.

sentences.zh: 八年，加通直散騎常侍、太子武衛率、前將軍，轉帥都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry, crown prince martial guard commander, and front general, and was transferred to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he received unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry, crown prince martial guard commander, and front general, and was made garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 東魏圍玉壁，綱從太祖救之。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei besieged Yubi, Gang followed the Grand Progenitor to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei besieged Yubi, Wei Chigang followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to the relief.

sentences.zh: 九年春，太祖復與東魏戰於邙山，大軍不利，人心離解。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year the Grand Progenitor again fought Eastern Wei at Mount Mang; the great army was unfavorable and hearts separated and dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai again fought Eastern Wei at Mount Mang; the army was defeated and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 綱勵將士，盡心翊衛。

translations.literal: Gang encouraged the officers and soldiers and devoted himself wholeheartedly to guarding and protecting.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chigang rallied the officers and soldiers and guarded the Grand Progenitor with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 遷大都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand commander.

sentences.zh: 十四年，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，加散騎常侍，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-to-three-division protocol, given the added title attendant of scattered cavalry, and his fief was increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol, given attendant of scattered cavalry, and three hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 俄遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵昌平郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand general of swift cavalry and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, given the added title attendant-in-ordinary, and advanced in nobility to Duke of Changping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand general of swift cavalry with opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, given attendant-in-ordinary, and raised to Duke of Changping.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out as governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was sent out as governor of Hua.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，拜大將軍，兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed Emperor of Wei, he was appointed grand general and concurrently commander of the guard army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the deposed Wei emperor he was made grand general and concurrently commander of the guard army.

sentences.zh: 及帝有異謀，言頗漏泄。

translations.literal: When the emperor had a divergent plot, words leaked out somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor plotted treason, word leaked out.

sentences.zh: 太祖以綱職典禁旅，使密為之備。

translations.literal: Because Gang's office governed the forbidden guard, the Grand Progenitor had him secretly make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wei Chigang commanded the forbidden guard, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had him prepare in secret.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝廢，立齊王，仍以綱為中領軍，總宿衛。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor was deposed and the Prince of Qi was established; Gang was still made central commander of the guard army and oversaw the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was soon deposed and the Prince of Qi enthroned; Wei Chigang remained central commander of the guard army and oversaw the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 綱兄迥率衆伐蜀，綱從太祖送之於城西，見一走兔，太祖命綱射之。

translations.literal: Gang's elder brother Jiong led troops to campaign against Shu; Gang followed the Grand Progenitor to see him off west of the city; they saw a fleeing hare; the Grand Progenitor ordered Gang to shoot it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Chigang's elder brother Jiong led troops against Shu, Wei Chigang followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to see him off west of the city; they saw a fleeing hare, and the Grand Progenitor ordered Wei Chigang to shoot it.

sentences.zh: 誓曰：「若獲此兔，必當破蜀。

translations.literal: He swore an oath, saying: "If I get this hare, I shall surely break Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He swore: "If I get this hare, Shu will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 」俄而綱獲兔而反。

translations.literal: " Soon Gang got the hare and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Wei Chigang brought back the hare.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜曰：「事平之日，當賞汝佳口。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said in delight: "When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said delightedly: "When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine mouth.

sentences.zh: 」及克蜀，賜綱侍婢二人。

translations.literal: " When Shu was taken, he bestowed on Gang two serving maids.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shu was taken, he gave Wei Chigang two serving maids.

sentences.zh: 又常從太祖北狩雲陽，值五鹿俱起，綱獲其三。

translations.literal: He also often followed the Grand Progenitor on northern hunts at Yunyang; five deer all rose together; Gang got three of them.
translations.idiomatic: He also often joined Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai on northern hunts at Yunyang; when five deer rose together, Wei Chigang took three.

sentences.zh: 每從游宴，太祖以珍異之物令諸功臣射而取之，綱所獲輒多。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed on tours and banquets, the Grand Progenitor would have the meritorious ministers shoot for rare and unusual objects; what Gang obtained was always more.
translations.idiomatic: At tours and banquets Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai would have the meritorious ministers shoot for rare objects; Wei Chigang always won the most.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，綱以親戚掌禁兵，除小司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Gang, as a kinsman holding the forbidden troops, was appointed junior minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, Wei Chigang, as a kinsman commanding the forbidden troops, was made junior minister of war.

sentences.zh: 又與晉公護廢帝，語在《護傳》。

translations.literal: He also together with Duke of Jin Hu deposed the emperor; the account is in the Biography of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu depose the emperor; the account is in the Biography of Hu.

sentences.zh: 世宗卽位，進位柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was advanced in rank to pillar-of-state grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming acceded, he was raised to pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，進封吳國公，邑萬戶，除涇州總管、五州十一防諸軍事、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Wu state with a fief of ten thousand households, and appointed area commander of Jing Province, commander of military affairs in five provinces and eleven garrisons, and governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng 1 (559) Wei Chigang was raised to Duke of Wu with ten thousand households, and made area commander of Jing, commander of military affairs in five provinces and eleven garrisons, and governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大長公主薨于京師，綱去職。

translations.literal: That year the Grand Princess died in the capital; Gang left office.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Grand Princess died in the capital, Chigang resigned from office.

sentences.zh: 尋起復本官。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，拜少傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he was appointed junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 1 (561) he was made junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 俄而授大司空。

translations.literal: Before long he was granted grand minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為陝州總管、七州十三防諸軍事、陝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he went out as area commander of Shan Province, commander of military affairs in seven provinces and thirteen garrisons, and governor of Shan Province.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was sent out as area commander of Shan, commander of military affairs in seven provinces and thirteen garrisons, and governor of Shan.

sentences.zh: 四年，晉公護東討，乃配綱甲士，留鎮京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Duke of Jin Hu campaigned east; Gang was assigned armored troops and remained to garrison the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu campaigned east; Chigang was given armored troops and left to garrison the capital.

sentences.zh: 綱以天子在宮，必無內慮，乃請出外，頓於咸陽。

translations.literal: Gang, because the Son of Heaven was in the palace and there would certainly be no internal worries, thereupon requested to go out and encamped at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chigang reasoned that with the emperor in the palace there could be no internal threat, and asked to go out, encamping at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 大軍還，綱復歸鎮。

translations.literal: When the great army returned, Gang again returned to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army returned, Chigang resumed his garrison post.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，以綱政績可稱，賜帛千段、穀六千斛、錢二十萬，增邑四百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, because Gang's administrative achievements were commendable, he was granted one thousand bolts of silk, six thousand hu of grain, two hundred thousand in cash, and an increased fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe 2 (567), for Chigang's commendable record in office, the court granted one thousand bolts of silk, six thousand hu of grain, two hundred thousand in cash, and four hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 陳公純等以皇后阿史那氏自突厥將入塞，詔徵綱與大將軍王傑率衆迎衛於境首。

translations.literal: Chen Gongchun and others, because Empress Ashina was about to enter the frontier from the Turks, an edict summoned Gang together with Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the border.
translations.idiomatic: Because Empress Ashina was about to enter from the Turks, Chen Gongchun and others had an edict issued summoning Chigang and Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 三年，追論河橋之功，封一子縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year, in retrospective recognition of merit at River Bridge, one son was enfeoffed as county duke with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, in recognition of his service at River Bridge, one son was enfeoffed county duke with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，薨于京師，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, he died in the capital, age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he died in the capital at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太保、十二州諸軍事、同州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted grand tutor, commander of military affairs in twelve provinces, and governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand tutor, commander of military affairs in twelve provinces, and governor of Tong.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Wu (Martial).

sentences.zh: 第三子安，以嫡嗣。

translations.literal: The third son An succeeded as legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: His third son An succeeded as legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至柱國。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached the rank of pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he rose to pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 安兄運，別有傳。

translations.literal: An's elder brother Yun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: An's elder brother Yun has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 運弟勤，少歷顯位。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Qin, in youth passed through eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Qin rose young to high office.

sentences.zh: 大象末，青州總管。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was area commander of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was area commander of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 起兵應伯父迥，事在《迥傳》。

translations.literal: He raised troops in response to his uncle Jiong; the account is in the "Biography of Jiong."
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops in support of his uncle Yuchi Jiong; the account is in the "Biography of Yuchi Jiong."

sentences.zh: 安弟敬，尚世宗女河南公主，位至儀同三司。

translations.literal: An's younger brother Jing married Emperor Shizong's daughter, Princess Henan, and reached opening-establishment equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: An's younger brother Jing married Emperor Shizong's daughter, Princess Henan, and rose to opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 叱列伏龜

translations.literal: Chilie Fugui
translations.idiomatic: Chilie Fugui

sentences.zh: 叱列伏龜字摩頭陀，代郡西部人也。

translations.literal: Chilie Fugui, styled Motouduo, was a native of the western part of Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chilie Fugui, styled Motouduo, came from the western part of Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 世為部落大人。

translations.literal: For generations the family were tribal chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been tribal chieftains.

sentences.zh: 魏初入附，遂世為第一領民酋長。

translations.literal: When Wei first submitted and joined, the family thereupon for generations held the post of first tribally enrolled chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei first received them, the family for generations held the post of first tribally enrolled chieftain.

sentences.zh: 至龜，容貌瑰偉，腰帶十圍，進止詳雅，兼有武藝。

translations.literal: By the time of Gui, his appearance was magnificent, his belt ten arm-spans around, his bearing in movement and rest refined and elegant, and he also possessed martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: By Fugui's time he was magnificent in appearance, with a belt ten arm-spans around, refined and dignified in bearing, and skilled in arms.

sentences.zh: 嗣父業，復為領民酋長。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's position and again became tribally enrolled chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post and again became tribally enrolled chieftain.

sentences.zh: 魏正光五年，廣陽王深北征，請龜為甯朔將軍，委以帳內兵事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang of Wei, Prince Guangyang Shen campaigned north; he requested Gui as General Who Pacifies the North and entrusted him with military affairs within the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Zhengguang 5 (524), when Prince Guangyang Shen campaigned north, he asked for Fugui as general who pacifies the north and entrusted him with headquarters military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋除善無郡守。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made governor of Shanwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Shanwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝昌三年，又除別將，從長孫稚西征。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang, he was again removed and made separate commander, following Changsun Zhi on the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang 3 (527) he was made separate commander and followed Changsun Zhi on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 以戰功，累遷征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For battle merit, he was progressively transferred to general who campaigns west and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: For battlefield merit he rose in stages to general who campaigns west and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後還洛，授都督，遂為齊神武所寵任，加授大都督。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Luoyang, was granted commander, and thereupon was favored and entrusted by Qi Shenwu, with additional appointment as grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to Luoyang, was made commander, and came under the favor of Gao Huan, who additionally made him grand commander.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，隨例來降。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Shaya, he surrendered according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Shaya he surrendered as others had done.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其豪門，解縛禮之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, because he was of a great house, released his bonds and treated him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, because he came from a great house, had his bonds cut and received him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 仍以邵惠公女妻之。

translations.literal: He also gave him Duke Hui of Shao's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave him a daughter of Duke Hui of Shao Yuwen Hao in marriage.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，封長樂縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Changle county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 4 (538) he was enfeoffed Duke of Changle with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 自此常從太祖征討，亟有戰功。

translations.literal: From this he constantly followed the Grand Progenitor on campaigns and repeatedly had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he constantly followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai on campaign and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為北雍州刺史，加大都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he went out as governor of North Yong Province, with additional rank as grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent out as governor of North Yong, with the additional rank of grand commander.

sentences.zh: 尋進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to general of chariots and cavalry, opening-establishment equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes, and attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to general of chariots and cavalry, opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes, and attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十四年，徵拜侍中，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，除恆州刺史，增邑通前一千四百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was summoned and appointed palace attendant, with additional rank as grand general of flying cavalry, opening-the-feudatory equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes, and governor of Heng Province; his fief was increased, together with the previous total of one thousand four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was summoned as palace attendant, with additional rank as grand general of flying cavalry and opening-the-feudatory equal in rank to the three dukes, and made governor of Heng; his fief was increased to one thousand four hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 子椿嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 椿字千年。

translations.literal: Chun, styled Qiannian.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, styled Qiannian.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: During Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed general of chariots and cavalry and opening-establishment equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shizong's reign he was made general of chariots and cavalry and opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 尋遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，改封永世縣公，邑一千二百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand general of flying cavalry and opening-the-feudatory equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yongshi county with a fief of one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to grand general of flying cavalry and opening-the-feudatory equal in rank to the three dukes, and re-enfeoffed Duke of Yongshi with twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，授幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he was granted governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 2 (562) he was made governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 天和初，除左宮伯，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianhe, he was removed and made left palace guard, and advanced in rank to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianhe he was made left palace guard and promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 閻慶字仁慶，河南河陰人也。

translations.literal: Yan Qing, styled Renqing, was a native of Heyin in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing, styled Renqing, came from Heyin in Henan commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖善，仕魏，曆龍驤將軍、雲州鎮將，因家于雲州之盛樂郡。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shan served Wei, successively holding the posts of soaring-dragon general and garrison commander of Yun Province, and thereupon made his home in Shengle commandery of Yun Province.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shan served Wei, rising through the posts of soaring-dragon general and garrison commander of Yun, and settled his family in Shengle commandery of Yun.

sentences.zh: 祖提，使持節、車騎大將軍、燉煌鎮都大將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ti was bearer of the staff of authority, general of chariots and cavalry, and supreme commander of Dunhuang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ti was bearer of the staff of authority, general of chariots and cavalry, and supreme commander of the Dunhuang garrison.

sentences.zh: 父進，有謀略，勇冠當時。

translations.literal: His father Jin had stratagem and plan, and his courage topped the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin was resourceful in counsel and unmatched in courage.

sentences.zh: 正光中，拜龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: During Zhengguang, he was appointed soaring-dragon general.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengguang he was made soaring-dragon general.

sentences.zh: 屬衛可孤作亂，攻圍盛樂。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Ke'gu raised rebellion and besieged Shengle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Ke'gu rebelled and besieged Shengle.

sentences.zh: 進率衆拒守，綿歷三載，晝夜交戰，未嘗休息，以少擊衆，城竟獲全。

translations.literal: Jin led the multitude in resisting defense; it stretched three years, day and night in battle without ever resting; with the few striking the many, the city in the end was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Jin led the garrison in defense for three years, fighting day and night without rest; though outnumbered, he kept the city intact.

sentences.zh: 以功拜盛樂郡守。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed governor of Shengle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made governor of Shengle commandery.

sentences.zh: 慶幼聰敏，重然諾，風儀端肅，望之儼然。

translations.literal: Qing in youth was clever and keen, valued his word, and in bearing was dignified and solemn; seen from afar he seemed imposing.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yan Qing was clever and kept his word; dignified and solemn in bearing, he seemed imposing even at a distance.

sentences.zh: 及衛可孤侵逼盛樂，慶隨父固守，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When Wei Ke'gu pressed and threatened Shengle, Qing followed his father in firm defense and contributed considerable effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Ke'gu pressed Shengle, Qing followed his father in the defense and did good service.

sentences.zh: 拜別將，稍遷輕車將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed separate commander, and was gradually transferred to light-chariot general with additional rank as director of attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made separate commander, then gradually rose to light-chariot general with the additional title director of attendance.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，拜步兵校尉、中堅將軍。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he was appointed commander of infantry and resolute general.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was made commander of infantry and resolute general.

sentences.zh: 旣而齊神武舉兵入洛，魏孝武西遷，慶謂所親曰：「高歡跋扈，將有篡逆之謀，豈可苟安目前，受其控制也！

translations.literal: Before long Qi Shenwu raised troops and entered Luoyang; Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west; Qing said to those close to him: "Gao Huan is overbearing and will have designs of usurpation—how can one be content for the moment and accept his control!
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao Huan raised troops and entered Luoyang, and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west. Yan Qing told his intimates: "Gao Huan is overbearing and will usurp the throne—how can we rest content under his control?

sentences.zh: 」遂以大統三年，自宜陽歸闕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon in the third year of Datong, from Yiyang he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: " In Datong 3 (537) he left Yiyang and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂慶曰：「高歡逆亂，宇內分崩，羣盜競興，入皆徇己。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to Qing: "Gao Huan is rebellious and disorderly; within the realm the state is split apart; bandits compete to rise; every man serves himself.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Yan Qing: "Gao Huan is in rebellion; the realm is torn apart; bandits rise on every side; every man serves himself alone.

sentences.zh: 卿遂能盡忠貞之節，重君臣之義，背逆歸順，舍危就安，雖古人所稱，何以加也。

translations.literal: You were able to fulfill the integrity of loyalty, honor the righteousness of ruler and minister, turn from the rebel and return in submission, leave peril and seek safety—though the ancients were praised, how could one add to this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you kept faith with unstinted loyalty, honored the bond between ruler and minister, turned from rebellion and came over, left danger for safety—though the ancients were praised, what more could be said?

sentences.zh: 」卽拜中堅將軍、奉車都尉。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed him resolute general and commandant of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon made him resolute general and commandant of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，以功拜前將軍、太中大夫，遷後將軍，封安次縣子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: At the campaign of River Bridge, for merit he was appointed forward general and grand master of palace consultation, transferred to rear general, and enfeoffed Viscount of Anci county with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At River Bridge, for merit he was made forward general and grand master of palace consultation, then rear general, and enfeoffed Viscount of Anci with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及邙山之戰，先登陷陳。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang, he was first to ascend and break the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang he was first over the wall and broke the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 拜撫軍將軍、大都督，進爵為伯，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed pacifying-army general and grand commander, advanced in nobility to earl, and given an increased fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacifying-army general and grand commander, raised to earl, and given five hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 慶善於綏撫，士卒未休，未嘗先舍，故能盡其死力，屢展勳勞。

translations.literal: Qing was skilled at soothing and settling; when the soldiers had not yet rested, he never first retired to quarters—therefore he could exhaust their utmost fighting strength and repeatedly display merit and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing was skilled at winning men over; he never retired before his troops rested, and so drew their utmost effort and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 累遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、雲州大中正，加侍中，賜姓大野氏。

translations.literal: He was progressively transferred to bearer of the staff of authority, general of chariots and cavalry, opening-establishment equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes, attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry, grand general of flying cavalry, opening-the-feudatory equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes, and chief rectifier of Yun Province; he was additionally made palace attendant and granted the surname Daye.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to bearer of the staff of authority, general of chariots and cavalry, opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes, attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry, grand general of flying cavalry, opening-the-feudatory equal in rank to the three dukes, and chief rectifier of Yun; he was additionally made palace attendant and granted the surname Daye.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐祚，出為河州刺史，進爵石保縣公，增邑千戶。
