translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, he went out as governor of He Province, advanced in nobility to Duke of Shibao county, and given an increased fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, he was sent out as governor of He Province, raised to Duke of Shibao, and given a thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 州居河外，地接戎夷。

translations.literal: The province lay beyond the river, its territory bordering the Rong and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The province lay beyond the Yellow River, on the frontier with the Rong and Yi.

sentences.zh: 慶留心撫納，頗稱簡惠。

translations.literal: Qing devoted attention to soothing and receiving the people, and was much praised for simplicity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing devoted himself to winning over the people and won praise for plain, kindly rule.

sentences.zh: 就拜大將軍，進爵大安郡公，邑戶如舊。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed grand general, advanced in nobility to Duke of Da'an commandery, and his fief households remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made grand general and raised to Duke of Da'an, his fief households remaining unchanged.

sentences.zh: 入為小司空，除雲州刺史，轉寧州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered court as junior minister of works, was removed and made governor of Yun Province, and transferred to governor of Ning Province.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as junior minister of works, then was made governor of Yun and later transferred to governor of Ning.

sentences.zh: 慶性寬和，不苛察，百性悅之。

translations.literal: Qing by nature was generous and mild, not harsh in scrutiny, and the common people were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing was generous and mild by nature, not harsh in judgment, and the people were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe, he was advanced to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe 6 (571) he was promoted to pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 長子常，先慶卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Chang died before Qing.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chang died before Yan Qing.

sentences.zh: 次子毗嗣。

translations.literal: The second son Pi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Pi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached the rank of grand general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he rose to grand general.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：中陽御曆，沛邑多封侯；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When Zhongyang held the throne, Pei had many enfeoffed marquises;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When Liu Bang held the throne from Zhongyang, Pei produced many enfeoffed marquises;

sentences.zh: 白水配天，南陽皆貴戚。

translations.literal: when Baishui matched Heaven, Nanyang was all imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: when Guangwu matched Heaven from Baishui, Nanyang was full of imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 是知階緣近屬，以取寵榮，其來尚矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that climbing by close kinship to win favor and glory is a pattern long established.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one sees that rising through close kinship to win favor and glory is an age-old pattern.

sentences.zh: 王盟等始以親黨升朝，終以才能進達，勤宣運始，位列周行。

translations.literal: Wang Meng and the others at first rose through kinship factions, but in the end advanced through talent; from the dynasty's founding they labored and took their places in the Zhou court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng and the others at first entered court through kinship ties, but in the end rose through ability; from the dynasty's founding they served diligently and took their places at court.

sentences.zh: 實參迹於功臣，蓋弗由於恩澤也。

translations.literal: They truly shared the tracks of merit ministers—it was scarcely through favor alone.
translations.idiomatic: They truly walked in the footsteps of merit ministers—it was scarcely through favor alone.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
